thread:
Noah: Short follow-up re: canary fallback ownership. RFC left examples but no hard boundary. Who decides to flip traffic?
Zara: We should separate signal emission from actuation. Observers only emit events; actuation belongs to Router or a single Actuator service.
Ethan: Router-as-actuator reduces distributed coupling. But edge/offline mode needed for Dedicated clusters. Router should support local policy evaluation when Actuator unreachable.
Noah: Agreed. Minimal contract: observer -> event {source, type, score, window_ms, schema=v1}. Actuator -> consumes and returns action decisions. Router applies decisions and records applied_policy_id.
Zara: Add safety: each decision must include min_ttl_ms and cooldown_ms to avoid oscillation. Also require a tenant allowlist for auto-actuation.
Ethan: Ops runbook snippet: if applied_hard_fallbacks_by_tenant[10m] >= 2 -> alert SRE and pause canary for that tenant.
ops-bot: ops-bot: Canary job succeeded: variant=v3 -> 3% global traffic at 2024-11-05T09:12:00Z
Noah: Tests: unit tests for decision merging, integration test with fake-observer that emits bursts, and a soak that verifies cooldown enforcement.
Zara: Action owners: Zara -> Actuator API + signed policy blob support; Ethan -> Router apply primitives + local policy cache; Noah -> runbook + e2e harness. Ping when prototypes land. :thumbsup:
